summary: Appends CHOP inputs one after another and optionally blends overlapping segments for animation, audio, and motion-channel sequencing.

key_params.name: blendmethod
key_params.note: Preserve length, overlap sequences, or insert blend region

key_params.name: blendfunc
key_params.note: Blend shape such as linear, ease, cubic, add, or hold previous

key_params.name: blendbyinput
key_params.note: Use first input channels to specify blend regions

key_params.name: blendbias
key_params.note: Favor previous or next segment during blending

key_params.name: match
key_params.note: Match channels by number or name

key_params.name: step
key_params.note: Shift next segment to begin where previous ended

key_concepts: Join CHOP appends multiple input CHOPs one after another and expects matching channel sets.
Later inputs are shifted so their start lines up with the end section of the previous input.
Blend Method controls whether lengths are preserved, sequences overlap, or an inserted blend region is created.
Blend Shape fades between adjacent segments or inserts interpolation curves between them.
Quaternion and translation blending provide special handling for rotation triplets and tx/ty/tz position channels.
common_gotchas: Join CHOP expects inputs to have the same channels; mismatches should be handled before joining.
The second and later inputs are shifted to line up with the end of the previous input.
Quaternion rotation blending expects quaternion attributes from Attribute CHOP.
Translation blending is aimed at tx/ty/tz triplets and can shift segments; use cubic blending if shifting is undesirable.
Add blend shape can be useful for audio but may increase levels.
